header_summary:
A new proposal introduces enhanced output script descriptors by embedding BIP39 mnemonics and optional passphrases directly within descriptors, thereby facilitating robust wallet recovery through standardized representation of derivation paths and script types. This advancement streamlines workflow integration, improves interoperability between wallet software, and supports secure multi-key and multipath setups. Further information and a demonstration implementation are accessible via the [pull request](https://github.com/polespinasa/bips/pull/2) and [Bitcoin Core repository](https://github.com/polespinasa/bitcoin/pull/8).

The Node Attestation Protocol (NAP) broadens stakeholder participation in signaling support for Bitcoin protocol changes by enabling cryptographically verifiable, coin-weighted attestations from economic nodes beyond miners. Attestations, distributed via peer-to-peer messages and weighted by UTXO value, are aggregated in a Sybil-resistant and privacy-conscious manner, though they remain non-binding and subject to privacy trade-offs. The protocol is implemented in [satd 0.7+](https://github.com/epochbtc/satd), with continued feedback invited and draft specifications available for review.

BIP54 introduces nuanced timestamp validation rules, creating a dependency between successive block timestamps while maintaining a conservatively wide acceptance window to guard against adversarial manipulation. Although theoretical attacks such as “slow-sliding-mtp” and “reverse header time hijacking” exist, their practicality is limited due to network decentralization and the narrow scope of potential exploitation. Additional discussion and technical analysis can be found in the related [mailing list thread](https://groups.google.com/g/bitcoindev/c/tKETFYnEtng).

Recent developments also include the deployment of two public libbitcoin nodes on testnet5, with monitoring tools and web explorers available at [Libbitcoin public configuration](https://libbitcoin.org/configuration/public.html), and the release of spscand 1.1.2, a privacy-focused, watch-only scanner for BIP352 silent payments ([spscand GitHub repository](https://github.com/ZenulAbidin/spscand)). Lithos Protocol further advances decentralized mining pool design by providing scalable, blockchain-agnostic infrastructure with streamlined payout mechanisms, as detailed at [lithosprotocol.org](http://lithosprotocol.org).

recent_posts.title: [BIP Draft] bip39() Descriptor Key Expression
recent_posts.summary: - A proposal introduces key expressions in output descriptors for improved mnemonic-based wallet recovery.  - Incorporating mnemonics and passphrases into descriptors enhances compatibility and security for wallet restoration.  - Details, draft, and implementation links are provided, with feedback welcomed on relevant channels.

recent_posts.title: spscand and libspscan: a watch-only BIP352 scanner
recent_posts.summary: - spscand enables privacy-preserving detection of BIP352 silent payments using multiple block source options.  - libspscan executes core cryptographic functions and is designed for integration without accessing spend keys.  - Security, privacy, and performance are validated through comprehensive tests, with code and support available publicly.

recent_posts.title: Testnet5 Launch
recent_posts.summary: - Two public libbitcoin nodes supporting bip54 are available for direct developer connections on testnet5.  - Node status and configuration details can be monitored through an online resource for participants.  - Web explorers are deployed to enable convenient blockchain data navigation and inspection on testnet5.

recent_posts.title: Open Question on a hypothetical minor "slow-sliding MTP" attack introduced by BIP 54
recent_posts.summary: - BIP54 introduces a new consensus rule tying certain block timestamps to their predecessors.  - Security margins and wide acceptance windows limit potential exploits, reducing risk from timestamp manipulation attacks.  - Theoretical attacks require over 51% hash rate but remain impractical and have limited impact.

recent_posts.title: Node Attestation Protocol
recent_posts.summary: - The Node Attestation Protocol enables non-mining stakeholders to publish cryptographically-linked, human-readable statements.  - Attestations are coin-weighted, non-binding, time-limited, and aggregated for transparency while addressing Sybil resistance.  - Participation increases network inclusivity but raises privacy concerns, with further improvements anticipated in later versions.

recent_posts.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
recent_posts.summary: - Lithos Protocol delivers a blockchain-agnostic, fully decentralized solution for distributed mining pool challenges.  - Its architecture emphasizes scalability, efficient coinbase output management, and streamlined payouts via atomic swaps.  - Secure, transparent block settlement is achieved through a trustless bitcoin relay across multiple blockchains.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal enables nodes to share stale tip information for enhanced Bitcoin network diagnostics.  - Technical design uses BIP 434 feature messages and restricts shared data for efficiency and relevance.  - This initiative aims to improve network health monitoring while inviting community feedback for refinement.

active_posts.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
active_posts.summary: - Strategies discussed include landmines, staked auctions, and Sats auctions for defending legacy coins.  - These mechanisms incentivize security through collateral, time-locks, and game-theoretic bidding structures.  - While currently theoretical, these solutions creatively blend cryptography with economic incentives for decentralized protection.

active_posts.title: BIP Proposal: ML-KEM Key Establishment
active_posts.summary: - A transport layer upgrade mechanism introduces ML-KEM-768 for post-quantum secure key establishment in P2P.  - Nodes can optimize bandwidth by selectively sending encapsulation keys; rekeying occurs after ciphertext exchange.  - Feedback is requested on ML-KEM parameters and default encapsulation key transmission versus bandwidth efficiency.

active_posts.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts.summary: - The proposal addresses vulnerabilities like timewarp attacks and inefficient transaction validation impacting network security.  - Suggestions include limiting legacy transaction size, restricting script usage, and invalidating insecure transactions.  - Some recommendations, such as reducing block size and standardizing elements, have sparked debate within the community.

active_posts.title: Unspendable keys in descriptors
active_posts.summary: - New miniscript and taproot integration raises challenges for creating practical unspendable wallet keys.  - Multiple key generation methods exist, trading off between indistinguishability, fingerprinting, and ease of use.  - Further discussion is required to refine solutions and balance security, usability, and descriptor standards.

active_posts.title: Propagation Delay and Mining Centralization: Modeling Stale Rates
active_posts.summary: - Block propagation times significantly influence miner revenue, especially favoring larger miners and promoting centralization.  - Simulations reveal that even minor propagation differences can shift stale rates and impact pool profitability.  - Reducing propagation delays can enhance decentralization and fairness in mining, supported by data visualizations.

today_in_history_posts.title: Ephemeral Anchors: Fixing V3 Package RBF againstpackage limit pinning
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Greg Sanders proposed Ephemeral Anchors to address package limit pinning for fee-paying Bitcoin transactions.  - The proposal enhances smart contract composability and prevents change outputs from being pinned.  - Open concerns include implementation complexity, miner extractable value, and effects on transaction anonymity.

today_in_history_posts.title: Mitigating Channel Jamming with Reputation Credentials: a Protocol Sketch
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Credential tampering by intermediary nodes can cause wasted value in classic payment paths.  - Routing nodes might unintentionally fail or cause accidental channel jamming despite no incentive for deliberate attacks.  - Effective channel jamming protections will leave only accidental failures appearing as apparent jamming instances.

today_in_history_posts.title: OP_EXPIRE: Mitigating replacing cycling attacks
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Replacement cycling attacks exploit HTLC scripts, prompting developers to adopt mempool monitoring and rebroadcasting countermeasures.  - Introducing OP_EXPIRE enables script branches to expire, improving contract security and reducing required on-chain interventions.  - OP_EXPIRE implementation involves encoding expiration in nVersion, yet community consensus on specifics remains unresolved.
